note: Independent same-scope rejudgment after reading RFC 8210 Sections 5.2 and 7, the Section 5.8 prerequisite, both complete tagged test units and the current readLoop, checkStreamSequence, checkResponseIdentity and handlePDU paths. Section 5.2 requires initial-negotiation Serial Notify to be ignored even for an unexpected protocol version; Section 7 explains that neither its Session ID nor serial is useful before negotiation completes. The complete requirement quote, MUST level, existing enforced verdict and all four original covers (the two polarities on each of two test units) remain unchanged. TestRTRStartupSerialNotifyOfAnyVersionIsIgnored sends an actual version-99 Serial Notify carrying Session ID 0xBEEF and serial 999 through net.Pipe/readLoop before a valid Cache Response and End of Data. It requires readLoop success, EOF rather than any response byte, final Session ID 7 from the Cache Response and final serial 5 from End of Data. Its paired control sends version-99 Cache Response in the same startup window and requires errRtrUnsupportedProtocol plus an Error Report of type 10/code 4; the exemption cannot be widened to every startup PDU. The fixture correction changes only the End of Data Session ID from zero to 7, matching the opening Cache Response as Section 5.8 requires; it does not change the EOD serial 5, notify bytes, unsupported-version control or assertions. This removes a different identity error that would otherwise confound the intended successful sequence. The bounded cache script and joined net.Pipe cleanup are retained. TestSerialNotifyIgnoredDuringStartup separately calls handlePDU with the supported version and requires no error, no completion, no adopted Session ID or serial, and unchanged idle state/version. Its Cache Response control must adopt the offered Session ID and advance the exchange, rejecting a blanket ignore-all implementation. The handler delegates identity checks, then exempts Serial Notify from initial unsupported-version refusal and returns without modifying session data; the stream sequence check does not reject that control PDU before it reaches the handler. The current four discrimination records retain their original requirement, units, polarities, revert route and RTRSession.handlePDU producer. Main receipts c37ecb67 and c2575cdd for the stream unit, and 733c8d68 and fa2111e5 for the direct-handler unit, each show the named clean baseline PASS followed by the intentional producer-disable panic red and the exact recorded polarity. These observations establish that the named units reach the producer; they are not normal-return semantic mutations and do not individually isolate the Serial Notify exemption. No new discrimination credit or broader protocol claim is inferred. The two independent handwritten 8210bis observations and the six existing RFC6810 version-0 unimplemented judgments remain separate; this rejudgment changes neither their scope nor their verdicts.
